note: Adapted from Light & Wilson's 1936 original description (in English), original name Nasutitermes chapmani sp. nov., in the paper on Philippine nasute termites; includes the alate (dealtated individual), soldier and distribution biology. The figures in the two original measurement tables are badly damaged in the scan; only head width 1.65 mm, ocellus-eye distance 0.040 mm and the soldier values head including nasus 1.38, head height 0.64, head width 0.99 and fore tibia 0.78 could be recovered, and the rest are not cited.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closest to N. panayensis (Oshima) and N. meridianus. The alate is larger than both, with relatively larger eyes; body colour much like N. meridianus, but the eyes are larger, the ocelli smaller, the cephalic hairs sparser, and the pronotum larger and differently shaped, while N. meridianus also has orange antennae and thorax. The soldier differs from N. panayensis in the smaller body, the almost unhardened sclerites, the paler head and the narrower head with a thicker nasus base; it differs from N. meridianus as above and lacks the orange head, antennae and sclerites of that species.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Alate (dealtated individual): head brown, postclypeus and labrum yellowish brown; antennae pale yellowish brown; pronotum yellowish brown; middle of the mesonotum pale brown to milky white; abdominal tergites chestnut-brown; sternites pale yellow with brown sides. Head shape as figured; head width (with eyes) 1.65 mm. Fontanelle prominent, narrowly triangular, opening anteriorly, about 3/4 as long as the short diameter of an ocellus. Ocelli oval, the long diameter about 1/3 of the long diameter of the eye, separated from the eye by about 1/3 of an ocellar diameter. Eye about 1/6 of its diameter from the lower margin of the head, about 1/4 of its diameter from the upper margin, and about 7/10 of its diameter from the posterior margin. The figures in the original measurement table are damaged in the scan and could not be recovered beyond head width 1.65 mm and the ocellus-eye distance of 0.040 mm, so only the legible values are cited.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier: head orange-brown; base and tip of the nasus darker; abdominal tergites almost unpigmented. Head and nasus shape as figured; head low, only slightly elevated posteriorly, the dorsal outline almost straight and only slightly wavy; nasus very thick near the base, tapering to a point at the tip. Antennae 12-segmented, about 2/3 as long as the head including the nasus; segment 3 longer than segments 2 and 4, segments 2 and 4 about equal. Measurements (mm, some digits damaged in the scan; only legible values consistent with the proportions are cited): head including nasus 1.38; head height 0.64; head width 0.99; fore tibia length 0.78.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Distribution and biology: of the 3 specimens, 2 were collected above Dumaguete, Negros Island, on Cuernos de Negros, one by Dr. A. W. Herve, then of the Philippine Bureau of Science, and the other by the senior author together with Dr. James Chapman of Silliman Institute (after whom the species is named), from a young colony in a dead branch.
